text:
emma: Quick check — weekly KPI thread. Saw a big lead spike in the dashboard after the launch posts but CR to MQL conversion dipped ~12%. curious whether this is real lift or noise.
raj: pulled the dashboard — traffic source = paid + organic social. paid CPA is up but volume shifted. looks like last-click attribution is crediting paid; possible double-counting from webinar signups.
maria: can you link the specific dashboard view? I want to check cohort by utm_content. I think webinar nurture pushed a separate landing which has a different conversion funnel.
emma: dashboard link: https://redwood.not-a-real-link/reports/launch-kpi?view=weekly
sophie: quick thought: the campaign's attribution window changed from 7d->30d for a/B routing last week. that could inflate leads but lower short-term conversion rate.
raj: good call. i ran a quick cohort query — slacked below.
raj: ```sql
SELECT utm_source, utm_medium, count(*) AS leads, sum(converted_to_mql) AS mqls
FROM inbound_events
WHERE event_date BETWEEN '2026-02-15' AND '2026-03-15'
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY leads DESC;
```
jake: results looked like: paid/social: 1,400 leads, 180 mqls; organic: 600 leads, 90 mqls. paid conversion lower but absolute mqls still higher.
emma: okay so paid is driving volume but lower efficiency. what about webinar registrants vs attendees? that might explain dip in CR if registrants are low-intent.
maria: webinar funnel: 600 regs, 220 attended, 70 became mqls. reg->attend ~37%, attend->mql ~32%.
sophie: interesting — reg->mql conversion is similar to organic, but paid regs have lower attendance rate (reg->attend 28%). suggests quality issue on paid audience or friction in reminder cadence.
emma: any signal on UTM tagging mismatches or landing page A/B that could cause routing to wrong nurture? we had an experiment that appended ?ref=rdw to some creative.
raj: found ~4% of paid leads with missing utm_content due to truncated click URL — they landed on generic campaign page and got default nurture. that could dilute conversion metrics.
jake: propose short fixes: 1) tighten paid targeting, 2) fix tracking param handling (engineering), 3) adjust webinar reminder sequence for paid cohort.
maria: agree. also recommend re-running attribution with 30d lookback and then a 7d sensitivity check to show bounds.
emma: can we get a quick viz for next weekly KPI review showing paid vs organic trends with two attribution windows? would help the exec summary.
raj: i'll produce both viz and the 7d/30d comparison by EOD. posting to the dashboard and sharing a short blurb.
nora-bot: Deploy report job complete — "launch_kpi_weekly_v2" dataset refreshed (rows: 58,213) :sparkles:
emma: awesome. also let's capture owner for each action: engineering (fix tracking) -> @sophie, paid ops -> @jake for audience tightening, comms -> @maria to tweak reminder cadence.
sophie: noted, i'll file a ticket for param sanitation and link it here when created.
jake: i'll run an audience prune and pause bottom-performing creatives today.
maria: i'll draft updated reminder emails and test subject lines — will A/B for paid cohort first.
emma: perfect. we'll review the updated dashboard + exec blurb in Friday's KPI review. thanks team :raised_hands:
maria: one last thing — any learnings for launch posts copy? conversion dip suggests performance messaging may be attracting high-volume low-intent. i'll sync with content to iterate.
emma: good call. add content sync to next week's agenda.
